column14: EPILOGUE, the potter: after university and seven years at an art publisher, near thirty he took up his uncle's path; he now does all the clay-kneading, yet still gets dizzy at the wheel

EPILOGUE, the programmer: 25 years on he writes control software for communications equipment at a big electronics maker; amid white partitions, grey carpet and never-sleeping fluorescent light he pictures those summer days running through the hills

EPILOGUE, the novelist: this is all he remembers of that summer; now a successful novelist in a New York hotel within sight of the Brooklyn Bridge, looking for the words of this story's epilogue; Shirabe and Moe are visiting from Japan for the 2001 countdown -- 'Goodbye, twentieth century'
EPILOGUE, the dam: within some fifteen years a huge dam was finished in the valley; where the uncle's house stood is 200 m deep in the rainy season; nothing is left to remember those days by
